_comment: Atlas Growth UK :: RECOVERY pass over excluded_officp.csv, mirroring clients/atlas-growth/recover-generic-config.json. The main config deliberately refuses the generic construction buckets because in the UK they are mostly general builders and would flood the list. This pass takes them back ONLY when the business NAME says foundation/damp/structural work — the pairing qualify-leads.js cannot express as a single rule. Deterministic, $0, no re-scrape. Run: qualify-leads.js --in <run>/excluded_officp.csv --config recover-generic-uk-config.json --out <run>/recover, then append recover/leads_clean_qualified.csv to the main qualified list (dedupe on place_id).

qualify_rules._r: 0. RECOVERY SCOPE GATE — recover ONLY rows the main pass dropped at its positive allow (drop_reason 'not_in_icp'). This is the rule that keeps a recovery pass honest: without it, the generic type net below readmits entities the main config removed ON PURPOSE. Concretely, a drain-jetting firm named 'Structural Drainage Solutions' typed 'Drainage service | Contractor' matches the generic type 'contractor' AND the name token 'structural', so it would come straight back through the front door it was just shown out of. Ditto a bodyshop typed 'Auto body shop | Contractor'. This works because excluded_officp.csv carries the drop_reason column that qualify-leads.js appends. CAVEAT: if this config is ever pointed at a file WITHOUT a drop_reason column (e.g. leads_clean.csv), qualify-leads.js skips the rule with a WARN on stderr and the pass silently degrades to type+name only — read the WARN line, it is not decoration.
qualify_rules.label: not_a_recovery_candidate

qualify_rules._r: 1. The generic type net. These are the buckets the main config's allow deliberately omits. In the 2026-09-16 UK profile, general builders with a structural-repairs line are ~17% of the real ICP — the single biggest segment the Maps-stage allow cannot see, because Google types them 'Construction company' and nothing else. Note this is an ALLOW, not a deny: a row carrying none of these types is simply not a recovery candidate and stays excluded. TWO TERMS ADDED 2026-09-16 (GATE 3, operator-approved). 'plasterer' (P5): UK damp-proofing is very often primaried Plasterer — re-plastering IS the second half of a damp job — and 39 UK rows with an ICP name token and >=5 reviews died in not_in_icp for that reason alone: Cheshire Plastering & Damp proofing Contractors (Crewe, 71), M.L Plastering & Damp Proofing Nottingham (88), L.R.Roper Plasterer & Damp Proofing (44), Dampguard & Plastering (Telford, 25), Wheatley Plastering and Damp Solutions LTD (25). Checked against the universe: 'Plasterer' is the ONLY plaster-bearing Google type string in all 21,898 rows (1,335 hits) — there is no 'Plastering service' category, so one term covers the population. 'surveyor' (P6): admits damp-SURVEY practices, and only ever in combination with rule 2's name gate, so a row comes back only when its NAME already carries an ICP token (damp, waterproof, timber treatment...). Substring-matched against the whole type string, so it also picks up 'Property Surveyor' (156 in the universe), which is how Prokil Chingford is typed. It CANNOT readmit a chartered or quantity surveying practice: 'Chartered surveyor' does not exist as a Google type anywhere in this universe (0 rows) — such practices are removed by the rule-3 NAME deny of the main config ('chartered surveyor'/'quantity surveyor', 32 rows) and by its rule-2 PRIMARY deny of 'quantity surveyor'/'land surveyor'/'building inspector', which give drop_reason 'name_deny' / 'off_icp_primary' and are therefore refused by rule 0 above before this allow is ever consulted. That is the whole safety mechanism for P6: rule 0, not this list.
qualify_rules.label: not_generic_contractor

qualify_rules._r: 2. The NAME must actually claim the work. This is the precision half of the pair — keep it strict. Tokens are the UK vocabulary from stageA_prefilter.py's NAMEKW plus the operator's list. 'wall tie' and 'crack' are in because crack-stitching and cavity-wall-tie replacement are how a UK general builder advertises structural repair. 'preservation' and 'remedial' are this trade's own words for the damp/timber side. Deliberately NOT included: 'restoration' (too broad — every stonework and water-damage firm), 'building' (matches everything), and 'groundwork' as a NAME token (a groundworks firm lays NEW foundations, which adjudicate/PROMPT.md classes as 'no'; it stays a TYPE-level candidate only). THE 17 BRAND_FAMILIES TERMS WERE ADDED 2026-09-16 (GATE 3 / P8, operator-approved) — all 22 term strings from the 17 families in atlas-growth-uk-config.json's brand_families, copied verbatim and lowercase so the two lists cannot drift. Reason: 78 brand-named rows sat in not_in_icp with a generic type this pass ALREADY accepts (Protectahome Ltd x6 typed 'Contractor|Surveyor', Prokil Chingford and Prokil Exeter typed 'Property maintenance', Timberwise UK Ltd Cheltenham, Kenwood Damp London) — their type passed rule 1 and they died here, because a brand name carries no ICP vocabulary. These are precisely the brands the operator's standing directive says to KEEP and FLAG, so failing them on the name gate contradicted the directive. Precision risk is nil: rule 0 still means only a main-pass 'not_in_icp' row can get this far, so a brand term can never rescue something a DENY removed — verified on fixture row 20, where Sovereign Chemicals Ltd (typed 'Manufacturer|Building materials supplier') stays dropped as off_icp_primary and is blocked from this pass, brand term or not. A brand is a flag, never a rule.
qualify_rules.label: name_not_icp

qualify_rules._r: 3. Same ghost-listing floor as the main pass so the recovery cannot sneak sub-floor rows in by the back door. (Rule 0 already blocks too_small rows; this is belt and braces for the degraded-run case described there.)
qualify_rules.label: too_small
